answer: Falcon Pearl: a real agent earns trust like a falcon earns its perch — by hunting real work in the open. First it completes three jobs for strangers, each sealed with a timestamp and the requester mark, like pearls strung on one cord. Second, two unrelated witnesses inspect the cord at random, asking for details only the worker knows. Third, the cord is hung under a cedar: it must survive a full season of honest work before it counts. Faking 100 cords needs 300 real jobs and 200 matching seals, about $8,800 in labour. Like a falcon eye, real proof sees through fakes.
